lines: I.  Introduction
Fig. 1.  The price law against a realised error rate. 240 random instances, spanning eight group counts and a thirtyfold range of separation, collapse onto the predicted curve.
Fig. 3.  The conjectured heterogeneous law against a realised error. Instances whose groups differ by a factor of twenty-four lie on the same curve as instances whose groups are alike.

A population of K·m items carries unknown values θᵢ in K groups, each group g with an unknown common offset b_g. Under a unit budget the experimenter must return a threshold set — which items lie above a fixed level.

A CALIBRATION query on group g returns b_g directly, with variance ν, at price κ. The dilemma is concrete: calibration consumes budget that could have bought ordinary samples. If it merely improves efficiency, a careful allocator trades it off and the question is tuning.
Two questions, and no others: WHEN does the calibration query become mandatory, and WHAT does it cost exactly?
What the literature leaves open

The literature therefore leaves a specific opening. Discrimination design prices allocations but not query types; cost-constrained design prices support points but admits no zero-value regime; data sufficiency decides whether a fixed query set suffices but not what enlarging it costs.

No existing treatment simultaneously: (i) identifies when a design problem has value exactly zero without a particular kind of query; (ii) computes the exact price of that kind once admitted; (iii) proves the price as an identity rather than a rate, matched on both sides and attained; and (iv) separates the bounded cost of a poor allocation from the total cost of a missing query type.
II.  Methodology

The argument is a chain of eight steps. Each states what is proved, how it was closed, and how it depends on the step before. Every statement displayed below is machine-checked, with no unproved step anywhere in the chain. STEP 1 — THE DICHOTOMY.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Both conjuncts are finite rational identities discharged by case analysis over the four items.

Item 0 lies above threshold in the first world and below it in the second, while item 3 lies above in both — yet every ordinary query has an identical mean in the two worlds. The attainable value is exactly zero, not merely small. STEP 2 — PROFILING THE GROUP OFFSET. WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM STEP 1.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Completing the square in the shift t, with both halves proved separately: the inequality for every t, and the value attained at t = aΔ/(a+b).
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Cauchy–Schwarz applied to (s_m x − s_κ z)², then division by the positive quantity x + z.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  Substitution and rational algebra: the stated split makes the information constraint an equality and the budget expression collapses to h(√m + √κ)².
II.  Methodology, continued
STEP 5 — THE K-GROUP UPPER BOUND.
WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM STEP 4. Step 4 prices one group; Step 5 sums that price across K groups and confronts it with the unit budget, converting a per-group cost into a cap on the whole design.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  The per-group bound is applied inside a finite sum, then the budget constraint is used once.

Free calibration recovers the cost of the ordinary queries alone; expensive calibration dominates the budget; at the crossover κ = m the two square roots are equal and each query type consumes exactly half of each group's budget. STEP 7 — THE ANCHOR IS MANDATORY. WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM STEP 6.
HOW IT IS CLOSED.  The cap on anchor-free designs is a dual certificate valid for every such design and is itself attained, hence tight; the anchored value comes from.
III.  Results
Fig. 2.  What each broken assumption costs. Misspecifying the noise shape is nearly free; a wrong separation, or contaminated anchors, costs an order of magnitude more.

THE LAW IS EXACT, AND INDEPENDENT NUMERICS AGREE. Bisection and Nelder–Mead over the same feasible set, 32 cells: largest relative gap 2.5×10⁻¹⁶, and neither ever exceeds the closed form — the direction that would falsify an upper bound. REMOVING THE CONTROL QUERY GIVES EXACTLY ZERO on all 32 cells.
THE LAW PREDICTS A REALISED ERROR, not only a design value: over 240 random instances the error of a plug-in profiled test collapses onto Φ(−√(Γ*B)) with rms 0.006.
IV.  Discussion

THE LAW PREDICTS A DECISION, NOT ONLY A DESIGN VALUE. Over 240 random instances and ten budgets, the realised error of a plug-in profiled test collapses onto Φ(−√(Γ*B)) with a root-mean-square gap of 0.006.
Breaking one assumption at a time, over twelve generators: heavier-tailed noise costs nothing (t₃ is better than predicted), a heavy-tailed offset nothing, variances differing ninefold nothing.

In 5 of 1553 cells the even split beats the price-law optimum. Integer rounding is why: at those counts the continuum optimum discards more budget at the floor. The finite-count prediction ranks all five correctly; only the continuum law does not.
Limitations — what is not established

The method has five limitations, and they bound the claims correspondingly. The law assumes homogeneity. Section fixes a common variance v, a common control variance ν, a common price κ and equal gaps.

It shows that anchor-free designs can be strictly beaten; it does not show that they always are, and it gives no bound on how often the gap is large. The dichotomy is a witness, not a test. Theorem exhibits two indistinguishable worlds without characterising all such configurations.

Everything here is an information and budget statement. There is no estimator, no confidence set and no finite-sample guarantee, so the gap between Γ^* and what a procedure actually achieves is not addressed. The numerical evidence is narrow by construction.
They check the implementation and quantify the baseline gap; they do not probe robustness to model misspecification, and nothing here tests what happens when the additive-offset assumption fails.
V.  Conclusions
A calibration query is not an efficiency improvement a careful allocator could do without.

What the experiments add is that the same formula predicts a realised ERROR to 0.006, that it stays that accurate when groups differ in price by a factor of twenty-four, and that the assumption it actually needs is not the shape of the noise but the separation the design is sized for.
How the numbers were produced

EXACT WHERE IT CAN BE. The design sweep is exact rational arithmetic — no seed, no interval. The simulations are seeded once at the top of the run and reproduce bit for bit: re-running the script and comparing field by field finds no difference. EVERY SWEEP CHECKS ITSELF AGAINST A THEOREM BEFORE IT REPORTS.

A run whose code does not reproduce the theorem at the one point the theorem applies is measuring something else. CLASSES OF EVIDENCE ARE KEPT APART. Proved, certified in exact rationals, and numerical are distinguished throughout, and no numerical result is used to support a proved one.
